answers.explanation: A fault is one component deviating from its spec. A failure is the whole system no longer serving users. Fault tolerance keeps the first from becoming the second.
You can't prevent every fault. You design fault-tolerant systems so faults don't turn into failures.
Hardware fails at random and independently, so you keep spares: redundant disks, machines, and data centers.
Human error is one of the most common causes of outages. Make mistakes easy to undo and limit how far they spread.
Chaos Monkey kills instances in production. Deliberately injecting faults is the only way to be sure recovery paths work.
Software faults are dangerous because they're correlated: the same bug runs on every machine, unlike independent hardware faults.
Data-intensive systems are assembled from databases, caches, indexes, and stream processors. Choosing and combining them is system design.
